objective: Rebuild AI navigation and article authoring around current research, one canonical paper, minimum concepts, and just-in-time foundations while allowing new current work to add only genuinely new lower-level foundations.

reader_contract.direction: current top -> canonical paper -> minimum concepts -> just-in-time foundations
reader_contract.history_stop: Do not recursively promote older cited papers when the reader already has the executable premise.
reader_contract.update_rule: Replace or add the current pointer first. Add a lower foundation delta only when a reusable mechanism cannot be explained, implemented, or diagnosed with the existing floor.

all_required: the current work changes a computation, data, runtime, or evidence contract
the existing concept floor cannot explain the new claim honestly
the reader must calculate, implement, or diagnose the mechanism
the mechanism is reusable beyond one checkpoint or product name
reject_examples: new product name with the same Transformer contract
historical priority without a new reader capability

deltas: hybrid or sparse attention candidate-selection contract

primary_sources.source: DeepSeek-V3.2 technical report and official release
primary_sources.intent: Reconstruct sparse attention, stable RL runtime parity, synthetic agent environments, and context management as separate falsifiable contracts.
Anchor current reasoning RL above the InstructGPT and PPO floor.
Place current concept-driven segmentation above the ResNet representation floor.
Expose current document parsing and verification above the Donut floor.
Keep model, harness, tool, environment, and evaluation boundaries explicit above ReAct.
Attach current evidence to the DDPM score and reverse-process floor without creating an unbounded lineage.

events.observed: The sidebar named target fields, foundations, and implementation, but target pages did not declare one current source, one canonical stopping paper, or a lower dependency boundary.
events.inference: Readers could see categories but could not know what to read now, how far back to go, or when to stop.
events.decision: Create one current-first research route for each of twelve target tracks.
events.verification: All twelve routes expose four fixed stages and an explicit history stop at 360, 390, 768, and 1440 pixels.

events.observed: Recursively following citations created an unreadable and effectively infinite historical syllabus.
events.inference: Historical ancestry is not the same as an executable prerequisite.
events.decision: Keep one canonical paper per causal branch and hide older provenance below the declared foundation floor unless the promotion gate proves a unique capability.
events.verification: Every track records a stopReason; source articles remain opt-in rather than expanding the default list.

events.observed: A future current paper can introduce a mechanism absent from the existing lower curriculum.
events.inference: A frozen lower graph would eventually make current articles incomprehensible, but automatically expanding it would recreate infinite history.
events.decision: Add a four-question foundation-delta gate and label accepted additions as new deltas.
events.verification: The LLM architecture route exposes two deltas and states that name or score changes do not grow the foundation graph.

events.observed: The 23-page V3.2 report combines DSA, mixed GRPO, synthetic agents, benchmark harnesses, and context runtime in one release narrative.
events.inference: Repeating the release summary would mix architectural, optimization, data, and test-time claims and overstate what each experiment supports.
events.decision: Read the complete report including appendix and reconstruct six execution stages, five equations, four evidence slices, implementation checks, assumptions, and failure boundaries.
events.verification: The source article distinguishes the remaining quadratic indexer term, runtime route/mask parity, verifier shortcuts, harness limits, and context-cost limits.

events.observed: The new research article loaded correctly but did not show SOURCE DEEP DIVE because that coordinate was restricted to paper slugs inside foundation categories.
events.inference: Source reconstruction is an article contract independent of whether the article belongs to a foundation or target category.
events.decision: Treat both paper-* and research-* as source deep dives and enable the shared deep-article and math-annotation system.
events.verification: The DeepSeek article exposes the R / SOURCE DEEP DIVE coordinate and current-research detail text.

events.observed: At 360 pixels, the TopK plus attention equation scaled to 0.70 and the advantage plus importance-ratio equation scaled to 0.71.
events.inference: Each display row combined two semantic operations, forcing the Korean underbraces and fractions into unreadable horizontal compression.
events.decision: Split each equation into two named aligned rows rather than lowering the global minimum scale or adding horizontal scrolling.
events.verification: All five formulas render with KaTeX, zero horizontal overflow, no visible raw LaTeX, and scale at or above 0.75 across four viewports.

events.observed: One horizontal four-stage diagram would become clipped or tiny on mobile.
events.inference: The stable visual invariant is the causal order, not the horizontal orientation.
events.decision: Use a horizontal 7-track stage/arrow grid only on large screens and a vertical causal flow below that breakpoint.
events.verification: Four mechanism modes switch state with zero document and Viz overflow at 360, 390, 768, and 1440 pixels.

events.observed: Discovery candidates previously suggested first-new-foundation-paper placement and had no explicit mechanism comparison state.
events.inference: Automated discovery could grow the bottom of the curriculum before comparing a candidate to the current top.
events.decision: Attach candidates to a track, compare the current pointer first, and record mechanismChanged, existingFoundationsSufficient, foundationDelta, and final decision.
events.verification: A three-day dry run produced 65 candidates from nine sources with zero source failures and the new review schema.

private_transfer_gate.question: Given a later long-context MoE agent report, determine which claims change model architecture, sampling/training parity, environment generation, and context runtime; then decide which lower concepts must be added and which older citations remain hidden.
required_insights: separate current evidence from the stable canonical computation contract
distinguish O(Lk) core attention from the remaining O(L^2) indexer
connect keep-routing and keep-sampling-mask to the validity of policy ratios
test verifier and solution shortcuts rather than trusting outcome reward
separate benchmark model quality from harness and test-time token budget
apply the four-question foundation-delta gate before adding a lower node
private_transfer_gate.coverage: DeepSeek reconstruction sections 02-06 plus the route delta ledger provide every premise; the private question is not published as filler.

four_b_jobs: extract at most four claims from one paper section into fixed claim packets
explain one immutable equation and Korean annotations without changing notation
repair one normalized QA defect with a file allowlist
classify one foundation candidate using the four-question delta gate
nine_b_jobs: merge four to six claim packets into one section packet
design one interactive Viz with control, observable, invariant, and failure
audit transfer-problem coverage for one article
orchestrator_only: primary-source retrieval and full-document completeness audit
small_model_replay.failure_replay_order: observed -> inference -> decision -> changed artifact -> exact verification
